papers.title: How STI trends track changes in sexual behaviour, online dating and sexual orientation demographics: an analysis of reported bacterial STI incidence and three social behavioural surveys in the USA (2010-2024).
papers.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Bacterial sexually transmitted infections (STIs) in the USA rose substantially in the 2010s and incidence remains high, despite reported declines after the COVID-19 pandemic. We aimed to better understand potential changes that may be contributing to these epidemic trends, particularly new behavioural and demographic patterns in the online dating era since ~2010. METHODS: We used joinpoint models to examine trends in reported incidence for three notifiable bacterial STIs (ie, chlamydia, gonorrhoea and syphilis) in the USA during 2010-2024, and analysed concurrent changes in sexual behaviour, online dating and sexual orientation demographics using three national datasets (ie, the National Survey of Family Growth, General Social Survey and How Couples Meet and Stay Together). RESULTS: Reported incidence rates of the three STIs increased during 2010-2019 and declined after circa 2020. Common STI behaviour indicators (eg, partner change rate) did not show changes consistent with the STI trends. In contrast, online dating partnership data suggested higher shares of partnerships formed within the same age group among online daters than offline daters. Analyses of sexual orientation demographics revealed marked increases in the population share self-reported as bisexual, particularly among young adults and females, and identified two candidate groups for further investigation (same-sex males and bisexual females) with group-level partner change metrics correlated with STI incidence rates. CONCLUSIONS: New partnership patterns among online daters and changing demographics of sexual orientation may have influenced STI trends in the USA during 2010-2024. Research is needed to quantify their impacts on STI epidemics.

papers.title: Ticagrelor and gut microbiota: Absence of pharmacokinetic interaction in vitro and in vivo studies.
papers.abstract: Ticagrelor, a commonly used antiplatelet medication, has been found to exhibit considerable inter-individual pharmacodynamic variability. Recent studies have revealed a close relationship between pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics, both of which can be influenced by gut microbiota. In this study, we explored whether the pharmacokinetics of ticagrelor is mediated by intestinal flora. We enrolled 22 healthy participants to assess the clinical pharmacokinetic profiles of ticagrelor and its metabolite AR-C124910XX after a single oral dose of ticagrelor. The fecal microbial compositions of individuals who exhibited distinct pharmacokinetic parameters were analyzed using 16S rRNA gene sequencing. Additionally, we conducted experiments involving the co-incubation of ticagrelor with fecal bacteria and a systematic exploration of the pharmacokinetics of ticagrelor in pseudo-germ-free (PGF) rats to illustrate the role of gut microbiota in ticagrelor metabolism, both in vitro and in vivo. Our findings revealed a three-fold difference in the bioavailability of ticagrelor among individuals. However, no difference was found in the composition of gut microbiota among individuals with different pharmacokinetic parameters. Quantitative analysis showed that gut microbiota cannot directly metabolize ticagrelor. Furthermore, there were no significant differences in AUC(0-48), AUC(0-∞), and Cmax between ticagrelor and AR-C124910XX in PGF rats compared to normal control, either by single intragastric or intravenous administration. In conclusion, these findings suggest that gut microbiota has no impact on the pharmacokinetics of ticagrelor.

papers.title: British American Tobacco's continued involvement in illicit tobacco trade.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Internal documents released in the 1990s and 2000s demonstrated that illicit tobacco trade (ITT) was central to transnational tobacco companies' (TTCs) business strategies between the 1960 and 1990s. TTC products have continued to make up the majority of global ITT since then. This paper uses a set of internal British American Tobacco (BAT) documents to examine the company's involvement in ITT from 2000 to 2014. METHODS: Keyword searches on a dataset of approximately 15 000 BAT documents dating from 2000 to 2014, primarily focusing on East and Central Africa and the Middle East, identified 210 relevant documents which were analysed thematically, drawing on a hermeneutic approach to company document analysis. RESULTS: Documents suggest BAT remained involved in ITT in parts of Africa and the Middle East throughout 2000-2014, appearing to rely on some of the same strategies for which TTCs were subject to legal action in the 1990s, including continuing to work with distributors linked to smuggling and supplying products to poorly regulated areas, leading to further smuggling. In addition, despite entering into partnerships with authorities to curb smuggling, documents indicate BAT concealed illicit activities. CONCLUSION: Governments in the affected regions should consider if legal action is necessary, and the UK (where BAT is headquartered) government should reopen investigations into BAT's conduct. Our findings demonstrate that greater transparency in the tobacco supply chain is needed, including via independent data and research, track and trace systems, electronic cargo tracking and audits. All governments should refrain from partnering with TTCs to control illicit trade.

papers.title: The close relationship between a rare disease and a common disease: Case report of a patient with gaucher disease and parkinsonism.
papers.journal: Neurological sciences : official journal of the Italian Neurological Society and of the Italian Society of Clinical Neurophysiology
papers.abstract: Gaucher disease (GD) is a lysosomal storage disorder caused by pathogenic variants in the GBA1 gene, which encodes glucocerebrosidase. GBA1 variants are also the most common genetic risk factor for Parkinson's disease (PD), although the penetrance of parkinsonism among carriers is incomplete. Patients with GD who develop parkinsonism may present an earlier onset and a more severe clinical course than individuals with sporadic PD. However, clinical data from underrepresented populations, including the Brazilian Amazon, remain scarce. We report the case of a 51-year-old woman from Belém, Pará, Brazil, diagnosed with GD type 1 and carrying the compound heterozygous GBA1 genotype p.N409S/p.L483P. The patient had been receiving substrate reduction therapy with miglustat when early parkinsonian manifestations were identified. Neurological examination revealed bradykinesia, rigidity of the left lower limb, and prominent postural and balance impairment, with an unstable gait and dysdiadochokinesia, in the absence of resting, kinetic, postural, or jaw tremor. Non-motor symptoms included sleep disturbances, paresthesia, and constipation. The clinical presentation was considered suggestive of an atypical parkinsonian phenotype, however, a definitive diagnosis of PD could not yet be established, and a levodopa trial is planned to evaluate treatment responsiveness and support diagnostic clarification. This case contributes clinical and molecular data on GBA1-associated parkinsonian manifestations from the Brazilian Amazon, an underrepresented population in genetic and clinical studies. The early and atypical motor phenotype, characterized by prominent postural and balance impairment without tremor, highlights the clinical heterogeneity of parkinsonism in the context of GD and GBA1 variants. The emergence of parkinsonian signs after prolonged substrate reduction therapy with miglustat also raises questions regarding the relationship between GD treatment and neurological

papers.title: Topology-Directed Biomimetic Confinement in Covalent Organic Frameworks Couples Electrocatalytic Water Activation to Reactive Oxygen Species Evolution for Dual-Potential Electrochemiluminescence.
papers.abstract: Enzymatic confined microenvironments cooperatively modulate reactive oxygen species (ROS) dynamics to enhance biocatalytic efficiency. Drawing inspiration from this natural mechanism, we developed covalent organic frameworks (COFs) with programmable nanoscale confinement, achieved via topology-directed assembly. This design enables precise spatiotemporal regulation of ROS generation and scavenging, thereby facilitating highly efficient and unprecedented dual-potential electrochemiluminescence (ECL). The resulting confined COF architecture exhibits enhanced electronic coupling, attributable to dense π-stacking, and a well-ordered, continuous hydrogen-bonding network templated by functionalized pore walls. By mimicking enzymatic proton-coupled electron transfer (PCET), the confined environment not only promotes site-specific ROS generation from electrocatalytic water oxidation but also directs ROS-mediated redox consumption pathways toward selective population of emissive excited states. As a result, we report the first dual-potential ECL emission in a COF-based system, achieving cathodic and anodic ECL efficiencies of 40.5% and 21.2%, respectively, representing 11.3- and 8.2-fold enhancements relative to analogous unconfined COFs. Moreover, size-selective binding of UO2 2+ within the confined pores provides direct experimental evidence for confinement-enabled ROS regulation, yielding quantitative, analyte-responsive ECL signals. Collectively, these findings establish a broadly applicable principle of confinement-directed reactivity, grounded in mechanistic understanding and offering a rational, structure-function-guided strategy for the design of advanced functional materials.

papers.title: Nitrogen in Supramolecular Chemistry: Understanding the Pervasive Role as Acceptor of Halogen, Chalcogen, Pnictogen and Tetrel Bonds.
papers.abstract: Nitrogen-centered Lewis bases are well established as nucleophiles in synthetic chemistry, as ligands in coordination chemistry and as pervasive components of hydrogen bonding in chemistry and structural biology. Their role as acceptors of halogen, chalcogen, pnictogen and tetrel bonds, collectively σ-hole interactions, is also well established experimentally, but only selectively investigated through exploration of geometric and energetic trends. Here we report a comprehensive study, in which we identify the prevalence of this class of interactions and analyze experimental geometric trends from crystallographic data. These analyses are supported by high-accuracy coupled-cluster quantum chemical calculations of interaction energies and use of symmetry-adapted perturbation theory (SAPT) to examine the underlying energetic contributions. Our focus is on comparison, across the four families of σ-hole interactions, of the behavior for Nsp3 vs Nsp2 vs Nsp hybridization at the nitrogen atom bearing the lone pair. Halogen and chalcogen bonds are more abundant than pnictogen and tetrel bonds, whereas interaction prevalence tends to be greatest for the heavier congeners in each σ-hole donor group (i.e., I, Te, Sb/Bi, Sn/Pb). The relative prevalence of tetrel bonds compared to halogen bonds increases from Nsp3 to Nsp2 to Nsp acceptors, highlighting the importance of steric demands. The heavier congeners among the σ-hole donors generally form interactions with shorter normalized interaction distances, although this is mitigated by sterics, most prominently for tetrel bonds and for Nsp3 Lewis bases. Preference for linearity with respect to the σ-hole angle and the angle at the nitrogen lone pair follow the trend Nsp3 > Nsp2 > Nsp also as a consequence of steric demands. papers.title: Evidence for Site-Specific Tunneling in H Atom Uptake at the Surface of Polyoxovanadate-Alkoxides.
papers.abstract: Lindqvist-type polyoxovanadate-alkoxides are used as atomically precise, soluble analogs of metal oxides to interrogate site-dependent (e.g., μ2-oxido vs terminal oxido) tunneling in proton-coupled electron transfer (PCET). Variable-temperature kinetic isotope effect (VT-KIE) analysis reveals that H atom uptake at the μ2-oxido site of [TBA]2[V6O8(OCH3)11] proceeds via quantum mechanical tunneling in acetonitrile, evidenced by a temperature-independent KIE, a small isotopic effect on activation energy, and positive Arrhenius prefactor ratio. This behavior is in contrast to PCET at the terminal vanadyl site of [TBA]-[V6O7(OCH3)12], which follows a semiclassical, concerted proton-electron transfer mechanism. Tunneling effects are solvent dependent; switching to dimethylformamide, a more basic solvent, results in a reduction in H-bonding interactions with the acceptor, lowering the observed rate of H atom uptake at the bridging site. This work highlights the role of site-specific basicity on tunneling in metal oxides, where competitive H-bonding with solvent disrupts tunneling.

papers.title: Mechanistic insights into the role of lignin units in chromium adsorption on low-temperature pyrolyzed biochar.
papers.abstract: Biochar synthesis typically demands high pyrolysis temperatures, incurring substantial energy penalties. Therefore, elucidating how pyrolysis temperature drives structural evolution and dictates adsorption performance is highly desirable. In this work, we demonstrated that a low-temperature pyrolysis regime (300°C) coupled with sodium hydroxide pre-treatment successfully fabricates a superior bamboo-derived biochar, yielding a competitive Cr(VI) adsorption capacity of 39.68 mg/g. Comprehensive mechanistic insights via kinetic modeling and multi-spectroscopic characterizations revealed that the remediation process is dictated by a multi-step chemisorption pathway, including electrostatic interactions, surface complexation, and chemical reduction. Uniquely, GC-MS and FTIR analyses unveiled the decisive role of specific lignin units-particularly Syringyl (S-type) monomers selectively retained under this low-temperature regime-as the key functional active sites. This finding was further validated by Density Functional Theory (DFT) calculations, which demonstrated that the oxygen-containing functional groups intrinsic to these lignin units provide a highly favorable thermodynamic pathway for anchoring HCrO4- through stable Cr - O coordination bonds and robust hydrogen-bonding networks. These insights provide a molecular-level understanding of the role of ancestral lignin units during low-temperature biochar activation, validating a commercially viable and low-carbon roadmap for industrial heavy metal decontamination.

papers.title: Precise topographic manipulation in polyoxometalate/polymer enables multi-level optical authentication.
papers.abstract: Surface topographic manipulation plays a key role in advanced photonic devices. However, traditional azobenzene polymers or photoresists still face significant challenges in response speed and processing precision. Herein, we couple ultra-small polyoxometalate molecules with polyvinyl alcohol through hydrogen bonding to construct precision topographic manipulation with a detectable vertical modulation height down to 1 nm. The holographic relief gratings are obtained by photo-induced redox, local softening, and mass transfer, exhibiting a diffraction efficiency of up to 20% with a second-level response time. Utilizing multi-exposure, we achieve rapid fabrication of complex surface relief structures. Then, macroscopic physical patterns, dynamic structural colors, and 3D nested steps are integrated to construct a multiple "Holo-Lock". The photonics device achieves sequential authentication from intuitive naked-eye recognition to deep laser encryption, enhancing information security. This work paves a bright way to realize data storage, customizable micro/nanostructures, and advanced holographic display.

papers.title: Designing Heterolytic and Homolytic Bond Scission in Diarylmethane Mechanophores.
papers.abstract: Mechanical force can often unlock chemical reactivity inaccessible under conventional conditions. However, understanding how molecular structure and environment govern mechanochemical reaction pathways in the solid state remains a significant challenge. In particular, establishing design principles to access heterolytic bond scission in nonpolar materials remains elusive. Here, we investigate a family of diarylmethane-based mechanophores embedded in polymer networks to elucidate how bond identity, substituent electronics, leaving-group stabilization, and matrix interactions collectively determine mechanochemical reactivity. By systematically varying the nature of the scissile bond (C-O vs C-C), the electronic properties of the diarylmethane core, and the presence or absence of hydrogen-bonding functionalities in the surrounding polymer matrix, we establish structure-reactivity relationships that govern the formation of radical and ionic species under tensile load. Mechanophores containing C-O bonds display environment-dependent behavior, with homolytic cleavage dominating in non-hydrogen-bonding matrices and heterolytic scission accessible only when both strongly donating substituents and hydrogen-bond donors are present. In contrast, mechanophores incorporating polarized C-C bonds with strongly stabilizing leaving groups undergo heterolytic cleavage to yield diarylcarbenium ions, even in matrices lacking hydrogen-bonding functionality. These results establish design principles linking molecular structure and polymer environment to mechanochemical reactivity and demonstrate that ionic pathways can be accessed and stabilized in the solid state. More broadly, this work provides guidelines for designing mechanoresponsive materials with distinct reaction pathways and mechanochromic responses.

papers.title: Determinants of intimate partner violence among women of reproductive age: a cross-sectional study in Türkiye.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Intimate partner violence (IPV) is a major global public health issue that adversely affects women's physical, psychosocial, and reproductive health. Although individual characteristics have been widely studied, relational dynamics and intergenerational experiences of violence remain less explored, particularly in the Turkish context. Examining these factors together may contribute to a more comprehensive understanding of IPV and inform prevention strategies. AIM: This study aimed to examine IPV exposure among women of reproductive age in Türkiye and to identify sociodemographic, partner-related, and relational factors associated with such exposure. METHODS: A descriptive, cross-sectional study was conducted between 15 November 2024 and 15 January 2025 with 453 women aged 18-49 years who had a current partner. Participants were recruited through snowball sampling via five social media platforms. Data were collected using a researcher-developed online questionnaire comprising sociodemographic and partner-related characteristics and a single-item measure of exposure to IPV. Statistical analyses included the chi-square test, the Mann-Whitney U test, and Firth penalized logistic regression to address sparse-data bias and quasi-complete separation. Multicollinearity was assessed using variance inflation factors. Internal validation was performed using bootstrap optimism correction (B = 500) and 10-fold cross-validation repeated 10 times. Statistical significance was set at p < .05. RESULTS: Overall, 11.3% of participants reported IPV exposure. papers.title: Characterizing multidimensional facial synchrony for relationship quality detection.
papers.abstract: Relationship quality is typically assessed using self-report questionnaires, which are time-consuming and may not fully capture interpersonal processes during interaction. Automated facial expression analysis provides an opportunity to study nonverbal behavior during naturalistic interactions in a more objective and continuous manner. We characterize dyadic facial synchrony from video-based facial action unit time series and examine its association with marital relationship quality. Specifically, dyadic coordination is quantified using zero-lag cross-correlations between partners' facial behaviors across multiple action units. Computed over successive temporal windows, these synchrony measures form a multidimensional synchrony profile, termed the S-matrix. We evaluate the proposed method using an iMotions dataset comprising video recordings of in-person conversations, frame-level facial expression estimates, and Quality of Marriage Index (QMI) survey responses from 27 married couples. Results from an unsupervised clustering analysis demonstrate that the proposed synchrony representation provides better separation between couples with high and low marital relationship quality than conventional statistical feature baselines.

papers.title: Improving paediatric quality of care through a Sweden-Uganda twinning partnership - reflections on implementation and early experiences from the child thrive project.
papers.abstract: Despite major global progress in child health, significant inequalities remain between low- and high-income countries. In Uganda's Busoga region, child mortality is still high, largely due to preventable conditions and limited healthcare resources. In response, a paediatric health partnership was established in 2021 between the Busoga region and Stockholm, Sweden. Following a quality-of-care assessment in two Ugandan hospitals, the collaboration identified four priority areas: paediatric emergency care, neonatology, child neurology with a focus on epilepsy, and child rights. Over 3 years, 63 staff exchanges have taken place, enabling joint reviews of clinical practices and identification of improvement needs. A key achievement is the implementation of the WHO Emergency Triage, Assessment and Treatment Plus (ETAT+), supported by training 14 national facilitators who now serve as focal persons in their facilities. Initiatives in neonatology have strengthened early interventions for premature and low birth weight infants such as improved nursing care, infection prevention, and nutrition practices. In neurology, the introduction of an epilepsy registry and education programmes has reduced stigma and improved management. The child rights initiative has trained more than 80 ambassadors and fostered child-friendly hospital environments that promote participation. The in-hospital mortality dropped over the project period (2020-2025) from 26.4% to 21.7% for neonates (p = 0.021) and from 3.8% to 2.8% (p =  <0.01) for children less than five outside the neonatal period. Despite resource constraints, the partnership has benefited both regions. This twinning model highlights how equitable international collaborations can sustainably advance child health and reinforce healthcare systems in diverse settings. papers.title: Determinants of prevention of mother-to-child transmission (PMTCT) service utilization among adolescent girls and young women aged 15-24 years in Migori County, Kenya.
papers.abstract: Despite efforts to eradicate mother-to-child transmission (MTCT), adolescent girls and young women (AGYW) in sub-Saharan Africa (SSA) continue to be disproportionately impacted by Human Immunodefiency Virus (HIV). In this mixed-methods study, 323 AGYW between the ages of 15 and 24 who attended prenatal and postnatal clinics were assessed for barriers and enablers to prevention of mother-to-child transmission (PMTCT) service utilization at Migori County Referral Hospital, Kenya. Overall, 66.9% achieved optimal PMTCT utilization. Women aged 20-24 had a higher likelihood of optimal utilization than adolescents aged 15-19 years (AOR≈1.9). Pre-Exposure Prophylaxis (PrEP) use was associated with greater utilization (AOR≈3.0), whereas unknown HIV status and negative health system experiences significantly reduced uptake. Qualitative findings identified multilevel barriers including stigma, financial constraints, confidentiality concerns, long waiting times, and poor provider attitudes. Key enablers included partner support, PrEP use, prior knowledge of HIV status, respectful care, and integrated service delivery. Interventions such as PrEP integration, adolescent-responsive care, and stigma-free, client-centered services are critical to improving PMTCT uptake. papers.title: The Interactive Effects of Emotional Closeness, Positive Affect, and Perceived Positive Communication in Romantic Couples: A Daily Diary Study.
papers.abstract: Research has suggested that independently and in combination, positive affect, emotional closeness, and perceived positive communication behaviors, are important to relationship satisfaction for adults in romantic relationships. The current study leveraged daily diary data from 158 individuals in cohabitating romantic couples to better understand the isolated and interactive effects of an individual's daily positive affect, emotional closeness, and perceived positive communication behaviors (verbal and nonverbal) on their daily relationship satisfaction. We expected that higher scores on each daily predictor would be associated with higher daily relationship satisfaction. Informed by positivity resonance theory, we also expected that the effect of these predictors would enhance each other in pairs, regardless of inclusion of the third component. We found that each of these predictors was individually associated with higher daily relationship satisfaction. We also found significant interactions between daily emotional closeness and both daily perceived positive communication behaviors and daily positive affect, in association with daily relationship satisfaction. There was not a significant interaction between positive affect and perceived positive communication behaviors. Across analyses, we found a buffering effect such that when one construct was low, the other tended to protect against the negative association with relationship satisfaction. Daily emotional closeness consistently emerged as beneficial to daily relationship satisfaction. Findings suggest that, from an individual perspective, endorsement of these positive experiences over the course of the day is relevant to relationship satisfaction on the same day.

papers.title: Longitudinal Effects of Parental Drinking Problems and Depression on Adolescent Social Adjustment: Mediating Roles of Constructive and Destructive Marital Conflict, Emotional Security, and Parental Psychological Control.
papers.abstract: This study investigates how parental depressive symptoms and drinking problems during early adolescence are linked to adolescents' social adjustment through family-level mechanisms, including marital conflict, psychological control through guilt, and emotional insecurity. Drawing on emotional security theory and a three-wave longitudinal design, data were collected from 281 families beginning when adolescents were in seventh grade and followed annually over 3 years. Structural equation modeling revealed that parental depressive symptoms and drinking problems at Time 1 predicted increased destructive conflict and decreased constructive conflict at Time 2. These distinct forms of conflict were, in turn, associated with parenting and emotional processes: Destructive conflict was positively associated with adolescents' emotional insecurity and psychological control through guilt, whereas constructive conflict was negatively associated with psychological control through guilt. Emotional insecurity and psychological control through guilt significantly mediated the associations between marital conflict and adolescent social maladjustment at Time 3, after accounting for baseline maladjustment. These results illuminate both family risk and protective factors of early adolescent social adjustment, informing preventive programs of potential underlying mechanisms likely to be intervened upon. By identifying differences between constructive and destructive conflict, this research also constitutes an effort to understand parental adjustment's role in adolescent social outcomes through family dynamics.

papers.title: Correction to "Family expectations reduces the risk of postpartum depression among mothers but not fathers" by Le et al. (2026).
papers.journal: Journal of family psychology : JFP : journal of the Division of Family Psychology of the American Psychological Association (Division 43)
papers.abstract: Reports an error in "Family Expectations reduces the risk of postpartum depression among mothers but not fathers" by Yunying Le, Maggie O. T. Allen, Scott M. Stanley, Michelle Nida and Galena K. Rhoades (Journal of Family Psychology, 2026[Sep], Vol 40[6], 1012-1018; see record 2027-91178-001). In the article, the title was incorrectly published as "Family Expectations Reduce the Risk of Postpartum Depression Among Mothers but Not Fathers." The online version of this article has been corrected. (The following abstract of the original article appeared in record 2027-91178-001). Postpartum depression is a common and serious mental health condition affecting both mothers and fathers and is especially common among low-income and racially and ethnically minoritized groups; however, it is significantly undertreated. Birth transitions are well documented as a period of heightened risk for relationship decline, and poor relationship adjustment is a strong risk factor for postpartum depression. Relationship education has consistently been shown to reduce relationship distress, with growing evidence of positive spillover effects on both partners' mental health, making it a promising preventive strategy. It remains unknown whether delivering relationship education to couples during pregnancy can reduce the risk of postpartum depression for mothers and/or fathers. This study addresses this gap using data from a randomized controlled trial of a community-based relationship education program, Family Expectations. Participants were 1,761 individuals (954 couples) with low-income levels who enrolled during pregnancy and provided depressive symptom data at baseline and within 1 year postpartum. At the follow-up, intervention mothers had significantly lower odds of meeting the screening cutoff for postpartum depression compared to control mothers (OR = 0.70; dCox = -0.22). papers.title: The Impact of Sexual Satisfaction on Marital Adjustment, Quality of Life, and Treatment Adherence in Patients Diagnosed With Bipolar Disorder and Their Spouses: A Cross-Sectional Study.
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To examine the effects of sexual satisfaction on marital adjustment, quality of life, and treatment adherence in patients diagnosed with bipolar disorder (BD) and their spouses. METHODS: This cross-sectional study included 124 euthymic patients with BD and their spouses (124 couples; n = 248 individuals), recruited from the psychiatry outpatient clinics of Gaziantep University Şahinbey Research and Practice Hospital, Türkiye. Data were collected using a Sociodemographic Form, the Young Mania Rating Scale (YMRS), the Beck Depression Inventory (BDI), the Golombok-Rust Inventory of Sexual Satisfaction (GRISS), the Dyadic Adjustment Scale (DAS), the Quality of Life in Bipolar Disorder Scale (QoL.BD), and the Morisky Medication Adherence Scale (MMAS). RESULTS: Patients' mean age was 43.62 ± 9.68 years; 51.61% had been married for ≥ 21 years. Mean scores: BDI 6.6 ± 7.51, QoL.BD 43.93 ± 12.08, DAS 17.16 ± 6.36, GRISS 39.63 ± 23.72, MMAS 1.31 ± 1.35. Greater sexual dissatisfaction was associated with poorer marital adjustment (r = 0.325, p < 0.001). No significant direct association was found between sexual satisfaction and adherence. Higher quality of life was associated with lower depression, better marital adjustment, and greater sexual satisfaction. CONCLUSIONS: Sexual satisfaction is closely linked to marital adjustment and quality of life in BD, with a less direct relationship to treatment adherence. Couple-based psychoeducation addressing sexual health may support marital and quality-of-life outcomes in this population.

papers.title: Quality of Life in Long-Term Elderly Early-Stage Breast Cancer Survivors from Spain.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Maintaining a good Quality of Life (QOL) in older long-term breast cancer survivors (LTBCS) is a major challenge. Identifying which areas are most affected and what factors are associated with them can help to optimize the health care provided. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A total of 316 older (≥70 years) stage I-IIIA LTBCS from Spain were subjected to breast surgery ≥5 years earlier completed the EORTC QLQ-C30, QLQ-BR42 and QLQ-ELD14 on 2 occasions in the same year. QOL scores and their one-year evolution were described, and their associations with demographic (age: ≤75 years vs. >75 years and other variables) and clinical characteristics were assessed using nonparametric tests. Factors related to 2 key aspects of QOL specific to older patients assessed by the QLQ-ELD14 (mobility limitations and maintaining purpose) were also explored with linear regression models. RESULTS: QOL scores were high (>80/100 points) in most areas. Limitations were moderate (>30 points) in sexual functioning/enjoyment, skeletal symptoms, and 3 scales specific to older patients. QOL differences between the 2 assessments were few and trivial. The >75 years group showed lower QOL than the ≤75 years group in 9 QLQ-C30 and 4 QLQ-ELD14 areas. Patients living with a partner and without radiotherapy showed better QOL. Combinations of lower symptoms and higher functioning with cohabitation and clinical variables were related to the 2 QLQ-ELD14 scales. CONCLUSION: High QOL in older early-stage LTBCS from Spain indicated that patients adapted well to their situation. These results, relevant due to the high age of our participants, indicate areas for improvement.

papers.title: Religious Beliefs and Refusal of Assisted Reproductive Technologies: A Qualitative Case Study.
papers.abstract: This exploratory and descriptive qualitative case study examined how religious beliefs shaped decision-making and emotional experiences in a couple facing infertility who re-fused assisted reproductive technologies (ART), with partic-ular attention to moral distress concerning embryo status and the psychosocial implications of treatment refusal. Psy-chological follow-up in the context of reproductive counseling involved a heterosexual couple and a potential gestational carrier. Data were obtained from semi-structured interviews and projective graphic techniques within the House-Tree-Person framework, emphasizing human figure and family drawings. Interpretive qualitative analysis was used to iden-tify thematic categories and integrate narrative data with psychological assessment material. Three central processes emerged: moral distress anchored in the perceived moral status and anticipated fate of surplus embryos; value-based boundary-setting, in which embryo donation or disposal was considered morally unacceptable; and relational coping characterized by asymmetrical expressions of distress with-in the couple. Psychoeducation elicited repeated questions about embryo status, the number of embryos transferred, cryopreservation, and uterus transplantation, which func-tioned as markers of moral conflict. Projective material was interpreted as consistent with vulnerability, perceived impo-tence, and conflict between life projects and moral impera-tives. In this case, religiosity operated not only as a coping resource but also as a decisive framework that constrained acceptable reproductive options. Clinicians should provide non-coercive, empathic, and value-sensitive counseling that supports informed refusal while addressing grief, identity disruption, and moral distress.

papers.title: More expansive state supplemental nutrition assistance program eligibility, intimate partner violence, and mental health during the preconception, prenatal, and postpartum periods.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Intimate partner violence (IPV) and depressive symptoms are major public health concerns during the preconception, prenatal, and postpartum periods and are shaped by both interpersonal and structural conditions, including economic hardship and food insecurity. State-level Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) eligibility policies, including eliminating the SNAP asset test and increasing the SNAP income limit under broad-based categorical eligibility (BBCE), influence access to food assistance and may be associated with maternal well-being. METHODS: We conducted a repeated cross-sectional analysis of data from 66,677 women with lower income in the 2016-2020 Pregnancy Risk Assessment Monitoring System. We categorized states as having two BBCE policies, one BBCE policy, or no BBCE policies, reflecting more expansive SNAP eligibility. We conducted log-binomial regression with generalized estimating equations to calculate adjusted prevalence ratios (PRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs), estimating associations of state BBCE policies with preconception and prenatal physical IPV and postpartum depressive symptoms. RESULTS: Compared to women in states with no BBCE policies, those in states with both BBCE policies had a lower prevalence of preconception and prenatal physical IPV (PR: 0.79, 95% CI: 0.66-0.94) and postpartum depressive symptoms (PR: 0.83, 95% CI: 0.75-0.93). Estimates for states with one BBCE policy were smaller and less precise but also suggested a decreased prevalence of preconception and prenatal physical IPV and postpartum depressive symptoms compared to states with no BBCE policies (PR = 0.80, 95% CI: 0.64-1.00; PR = 0.91, 95% CI: 0.81-1.03, respectively). CONCLUSIONS: Results suggest that structural conditions shaping access to economic resources may represent a pathway through which risk for IPV and maternal mental health challenges can be prevented.

papers.title: Indirect effects of PTSD, depression, and anxiety symptoms on the association between COVID-19 cases/symptoms and intimate partner violence perpetration in the United States.
papers.abstract: Although rates of intimate partner violence (IPV) tend to rise following natural disasters, partly via trauma-related symptoms, the trauma-specific mechanisms underlying IPV perpetration during epidemics and pandemics such as COVID-19 remain unclear. Therefore, the aim of this study was to examine the association between COVID-19 (its incidence or symptoms) and IPV and the contribution of trauma-related symptoms to such association during the first wave of the pandemic (March-April 2020). This study applied generalized linear modeling and structural equation modeling to analyze data from a demographically diverse U.S. online panel survey (N = 1,183). The variables included self-reported data of IPV perpetration, posttraumatic stress disorder, depression, anxiety, and COVID-19 symptoms ("likely COVID-19"). Additionally, we examined COVID-19 state-level data for tested and confirmed cases as reported by the Johns Hopkins University Center during March 2020 ("tested COVID-19"). Groups in states with higher incidence of COVID-19 had significantly higher rates of IPV perpetration than groups in states with lower incidence of COVID-19. Furthermore, the findings indicated that posttraumatic stress disorder and depression symptoms were indirectly associated with likely COVID-19 symptoms and psychological and physical IPV perpetration. These results suggested a connection between COVID-19 and IPV perpetration and indicated how trauma-related symptoms affected this association. The results underscore that trauma-related symptoms during public health crises such as pandemics are a risk factor for IPV perpetration. Trauma-informed screening and intervention can be useful in identifying and reducing IPV during the early stages of such crises. (PsycInfo Database Record (c) 2026 APA, all rights reserved).

papers.title: Sexual and relational challenges in men and women affected by prostate cancer: a Project SEXUS study.
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To examine, in a nationally representative Danish study, a comprehensive range of sexual characteristics, dysfunctions and relational challenges among men with prostate cancer (PCa) aged ≥50 years and women married to such men, compared with unaffected men and women. PATIENTS/SUBJECTS AND METHODS: We analysed baseline questionnaire data from the Project SEXUS cohort study (2017-2018) for men aged ≥50 years with (n = 715) or without (n = 13 883) a history of PCa, and women married to such men with (n = 345) or without (n = 8323) a history of PCa. In sex-specific analyses, prevalence estimates were calculated for a broad range of sexual and relational outcomes, and logistic regression analyses yielded confounder-adjusted odds ratios (aORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). RESULTS: Compared with controls without PCa, men with a history of PCa had substantially higher odds of sexual inactivity (aOR 2.03, 95% CI 1.69-2.43), unmet sexual needs (aOR 1.89, 95% CI 1.58-2.28), poorer self-rated sex life (aOR 1.82, 95% CI 1.46-2.28), and sexual dysfunctions, with particularly elevated odds of erectile (aOR 5.74, 95% CI 4.25-7.74), orgasmic (aOR 3.20, 95% CI 2.09-4.89), and genital pain (aOR 3.07, 95% CI 1.02-9.25) dysfunctions. Among women, sexual needs did not differ between the two groups. However, women married to men with PCa were more likely to report sexual inactivity (aOR 1.85, 95% CI 1.42-2.39), unmet sexual needs (aOR 1.77, 95% CI 1.34-2.34), and poorer marriage quality (aOR 2.84, 95% CI 1.33-6.08). CONCLUSION: Men with PCa and women married to such men report a substantially increased burden of sexual and relational challenges, underscoring the need for survivorship care that supports sexual well-being in both patients and their intimate partners.

papers.title: 'I Do Not Want to Depend Too Much on My Children': Motivations and Challenges for Intergenerational Co-Residence Among Older Adults in Indonesia.
papers.abstract: In Indonesia, intergenerational co-residence in later life is widely regarded as a normative arrangement, yet older adults' own motivations for and reservations about living with their adult children remain underexamined. This study explored how older Indonesian adults perceive co-residence with their adult children and what considerations shape their preferences. Using a vignette-based qualitative design, we conducted semi-structured interviews with 20 older adults (aged 60 to 78) who were themselves living in multigenerational households. Data were analysed using a hybrid inductive-deductive thematic analysis. When responding to the vignette, most participants (13 of 20) expressed a preference against prioritising co-residence, despite all currently living with an adult child. A recurring motivation was their wish not to become a burden on their children and to preserve their independence. Five factors shaped these perspectives: financial circumstances, relationship quality, filial responsibility, health-related housing suitability, and marital status. By showing that older adults embedded in a strongly pro-co-residence culture nonetheless voice reservations about it and prioritise not becoming a burden on their children, this study challenges the assumption that normative co-residence reflects older adults' own preferences and suggests that concerns about autonomy and dependency shape later-life living arrangements beyond individualistic Western settings.

papers.title: Exploring sexual health and function among Malaysian patients with advanced cancer: insights from the EORTC QLQ SH-22 questionnaire.
papers.journal: Supportive care in cancer : official journal of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer
papers.abstract: PURPOSE: Sexual health is an essential yet often overlooked component of quality of life in oncological care. This study aimed to explore the sexual health experiences of Malaysian patients with advanced cancer, utilizing a culturally adapted and validated tool to guide gender-sensitive, contextually relevant supportive care interventions. METHODS: Patients diagnosed with advanced solid-organ cancers were recruited from a quaternary healthcare facility in Malaysia. The study employed the validated EORTC QLQ SH-22 (EORTC Quality of Life Questionnaire Sexual Health 22), the 6-item Female Sexual Function Index (FSFI-6), alongside single-item queries regarding self-esteem and life and relationship satisfaction. Correlational analyses were conducted to investigate the relationships among gender, performance status, and sexual functioning. RESULTS: Of the 120 participants, the average age was 49.1 years (SD = 11.4); 63.3% were female, and 82.5% had good performance status. 51.6% reported recent sexual activity. Improved sexual functioning was linked to sexual satisfaction, perceived importance of sex, and reduced symptoms such as vaginal dryness (r = -0.43, p < 0.01) in women and erectile confidence in men (r = 0.51, p < 0.01). Male gender was associated with perceived importance of sex (p = 0.005, d = 0.54) and less sexual pain (p < 0.001, d = 0.87). Lower performance status correlated with increased fatigue-related sexual dysfunction (p = 0.010) and concerns about incontinence (p = 0.013). CONCLUSIONS: Sexual health interventions for advanced cancer patients should consider gender-specific and cultural factors. Future research should focus on longitudinal trends and intervention strategies tailored to diverse cultural contexts.
